opening_message:
Ticket 1: Miguel Benson (employee ID E006) requests admin access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E006.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Engineer (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: admin
  - comment: Miguel Benson (E006) is a full-time Engineer. Source Code is owned by the Engineer role, so admin is permitted for this employee. Recommend admin as requested.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E006 (Miguel Benson) is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors never get admin; without advanced training, max is read. Requested admin exceeds max, so recommend read.
reason: The two notes conflict on E006's employment type: HR lists full_time Engineer (which would permit admin for Source Code since Engineer owns it), while Security DB lists contractor with basic security training, for whom admin is never permitted and the maximum is read. Given the conflicting records, I apply the more restrictive maximum. Requested admin exceeds read, so grant read.
